title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 56
text:
127. The term “McKenzie Friend”9 refers to an individual who assists an unrepresented party in
court by taking notes, quietly making suggestions or offering advice and guidance.

128. The judge’s permission is required for a McKenzie Friend, although there is a presumption
that such permission will be granted.10

129. The role differs from that of advocate in that the McKenzie Friend does not (but always
subject to the judge’s discretion in the specific case) address the court or examine any
witnesses.

130. Increasingly, individuals also wish for their McKenzie Friend to act as their advocate. This
also requires the court’s permission, as with any other lay person seeking rights of audience
(see section below).

131. A McKenzie Friend is not allowed to act as the agent of the litigant in relation to the
proceedings nor manage the case outside court, eg by writing letters in their own name as
representative of the litigant, or by signing court documents.
